storyboard.claim: The urge to clear the deck is a psychological mirage.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A woman at a desk stares at a full inbox, pondering.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the inbox-zero bit: the instinct is introduced as a trap.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the researcher's finding as a mirage before the research is described.
storyboard.staging: Everyman thinks with a worried face at a cluttered desk.

storyboard.claim: High performance is not about how fast you answer emails.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The woman pauses with her hand off the keyboard, rejecting speed.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the research result as a rejection of the speed instinct.
storyboard.addedInformation: Strike marks the narrator rejecting the speed-of-email idea.
storyboard.staging: Everyman sits still, hands off the keyboard.

storyboard.claim: The foundation is knowing your highest-leverage priority and doing it first.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A target icon, the single aim point.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the rejected speed idea into a positive rule.
storyboard.addedInformation: The target says aim at one priority, which is the MIT claim.
storyboard.staging: Everyman focused on the target icon.

storyboard.claim: Execute the priority before outside demands intervene; email gives a dopamine hit.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A smartphone, the constant interrupt.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains why the priority gets pushed aside.
storyboard.addedInformation: The phone shows the interrupt source the narration describes.
storyboard.staging: Everyman talks while the phone icon sits in frame.

storyboard.claim: Clearing emails feels like progress but is not.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The woman shrugs at a tiny completed item.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the fake-progress feeling of answering email.
storyboard.addedInformation: Strike marks the narrator rejecting the feeling of completion.
storyboard.staging: Everyman talks with a neutral face.

storyboard.claim: The big priority needs deep, painful cognitive friction, so people drift to easy wins.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A boulder sits in the path, the hard task.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains why people avoid the priority.
storyboard.addedInformation: The boulder reads as the hard obstacle in the way.
storyboard.staging: Everyman slumps in front of the heavy obstacle.

storyboard.claim: A rigid rule of the MIT comes from an Olympian's career.

storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the Olympian example as a host interview.
storyboard.addedInformation: The trophy reads as the status of gold medals.

storyboard.claim: She asked herself one yes-or-no question many times a day.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A woman pausing to ask herself a question.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Describes the filter the Olympian used.
storyboard.addedInformation: Callout gives the concrete filter form.

storyboard.claim: The filter asks whether an activity helps win gold.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A woman weighing an invitation in her head.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the filter question in plain words.
storyboard.addedInformation: Callout repeats the test in the narrator's words.

storyboard.claim: A night out that fails the filter is turned down.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A woman declining an invitation with a shake of the head.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Applies the filter to the drinks invitation.
storyboard.addedInformation: Callout states the decision.

storyboard.claim: When the priority is done is scientifically critical.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A clock, the timing of the task.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from what to do to when to do it.
storyboard.addedInformation: The clock shows timing, not just time passing.
storyboard.staging: Everyman thinks beside the clock in the office.

storyboard.claim: A behavioral economist studies when the brain peaks.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A woman speaking, presenting the researcher.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the researcher on peak cognition timing.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the researcher with the correct spelling.

storyboard.claim: The brain peaks two to three hours after waking.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A clock, the timing of peak focus.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the timing of the peak.
storyboard.addedInformation: The clock marks the window after waking.
storyboard.staging: Everyman thinks with the clock icon.

storyboard.claim: The golden morning hours get spent on scrolling and sorting email.

storyboard.onScreenText: Commutes and inboxes eat the golden hours
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the sequence of wasted hours.
storyboard.addedInformation: Flow makes the cause-and-effect path explicit.
storyboard.staging: Everyman slumps, the flow shows the path.

storyboard.claim: Using peak brain power for trivial tasks wastes a powerful tool.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A woman thinking about a small errand.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Extends the wasted-hours point with an analogy.
storyboard.addedInformation: Callout gives the analogy in concrete words.

storyboard.claim: Wasting peak hours is an astronomical waste of leverage.

storyboard.relationToPrevious: Pure commentary on the previous analogy.
storyboard.addedInformation: Weak: the picture carries nothing; the callout carries the claim.

storyboard.claim: A product leader must give half of work hours to the priority.

storyboard.claim: It is easy for a billionaire CEO to ignore the inbox.

storyboard.claim: The MIT works without full autonomy but must be defined differently.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A woman talking, reframing the idea.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers the autonomy objection.
storyboard.addedInformation: Callout gives the reframe.

storyboard.claim: The MIT is the highest-leverage action within your locus of control.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A woman talking.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the working definition.
storyboard.addedInformation: Callout restates the definition.

storyboard.claim: A junior sales rep's MIT is 25 cold calls before 10 a.m.

storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives a concrete MIT for a junior role.
storyboard.addedInformation: Callout gives the number of calls.

storyboard.claim: If the boss demands 8:30 email, there are two options.

storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sets up the two options.
storyboard.addedInformation: Callout announces the choice.

storyboard.claim: Option one is an MIT done in 45 minutes between 8:45 and 9:30.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A clock, the 45-minute window.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the first option.

storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the second option.
storyboard.addedInformation: Callout gives the action.

storyboard.claim: Refuse to let other people's emergencies decide when your best work happens.

storyboard.addedInformation: The shield reads as protection of the work.

storyboard.claim: Choosing your best energy is a decision problem, not a scheduling problem.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A woman pointing at the viewer.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Restates the principle as a decision.
